Participate is the third WHAT skill. Enter fully into the current activity instead of remaining only an observer of yourself.

## Participate in this moment {#participate}

Participation is present-moment involvement: joining the conversation, movement, task, play, creative work, or ordinary routine you are actually doing. Flexible, spontaneous responding becomes more possible when attention is with the activity rather than constantly monitoring every step. Sometimes immersion or flow occurs, but flow is not a requirement.

Participation does not mean losing awareness. It means acting with awareness rather than staying outside the experience.

## When participating is difficult {#when-participating-is-difficult}

Observe and Describe can come first. Pause, notice what is happening, put useful words to it, and then re-enter the activity. Use the mindfulness skill that fits the moment rather than forcing Observe, Describe, and Participate simultaneously.

Representative practices include joining a conversation, singing or dancing, playing a game or sport, cooking, making something, doing a household task, or following the movements of a familiar routine with full attention.
